=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: _segment_shape lines 179-214; _family_word lines 352-360 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: A separate-value global option before a subcommand, such as `-R owner/repo`, consumes the positional slot used to detect the subcommand, so `_family_word` collapses distinct commands such as `gh api` and `gh issue` into `gh`.
  WHY: CLAUDE.md §23.D requires `-R` on repository-context `gh` commands, causing distinct subcommand prompts to be grouped under the same family and filed on the wrong issue.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: _family_segments lines 279-303, specifically line 292, and _SHELL_PUNCTUATION_CHARS line 117 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: `_family_segments` checks for a `<<` token, but the configured shell punctuation splits `<<` into separate `<` tokens, so heredoc constructs are not added to command families.
  WHY: This reportedly makes heredoc and non-heredoc commands share a family, although the reviewer notes that a test asserts the heredoc family and recommends independent verification.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: _family_core lines 306-319, specifically line 318 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `_family_core` unconditionally skips a duration argument after processing `timeout` flags, so when the required duration is missing it consumes the command word instead.
  WHY: A malformed command such as `timeout -k 5 git fetch` is classified under `fetch` rather than `git fetch`, routing the logged failed attempt to the wrong family.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: _ISSUE_EXAMPLE_RE line 136; issue_family_marker lines 408-413; _occurrence_block lines 520-522 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: A logged command containing a line of four or more backticks can prematurely terminate the fixed four-backtick example fence, allowing family-marker text in the remaining command text to be treated as issue metadata.
  WHY: On a legacy issue, `index_issues` trusts the extracted marker before deriving the family from the example, potentially routing later prompts to the wrong family issue; reviewers describe exploitability as narrow.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: file_patterns lines 695-730 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Concurrent `file_patterns` invocations can each read an index without a family issue and then create a separate issue for the same family.
  WHY: In-memory registration only coordinates patterns within one invocation; this is described as a pre-existing read-then-write race with low practical likelihood because stage sessions are typically sequential.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: _segment_shape lines 198-213, _family_word lines 352-360 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `_segment_shape` only recognizes `-X` and `--method` as value-taking options, so a preceding value-taking global option can consume the positional slot used for subcommand detection.
  WHY: Commands such as `gh -R owner/repo api ...` and `gh -R owner/repo issue view ...` produce family word `gh`, grouping distinct subcommand prompts together; the cited test covers commands without value-taking global options.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: _family_core lines 306-319, specifically line 318 | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `_family_core` unconditionally skips one token after processing `timeout` flags, consuming the command word when the required duration is missing.
  WHY: A malformed invocation such as `timeout -k 5 git fetch` is assigned to the wrong family; the command would fail at runtime anyway, limiting practical impact.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: _family_segments lines 279-303, specifically line 292, and _SHELL_PUNCTUATION_CHARS line 117 | severity=high | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `_family_segments` checks `token == "<<"`, but the shell punctuation configuration splits `<<` into individual `<` tokens, so heredoc constructs are not added to command families.
  WHY: Heredoc and non-heredoc variants reportedly share a family; the reviewer notes that a test asserts the heredoc family and recommends independently verifying the discrepancy.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: file_patterns lines 697-727, specifically the gap between index_issues read at line 698 and issue creation at line 718 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Concurrent invocations can each observe an empty family index and create separate issues for different signatures in the same family.
  WHY: In-run registration only coordinates patterns within one invocation; the reviewer describes this as a pre-existing race with rare practical concurrency.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: _ISSUE_EXAMPLE_RE line 136, issue_family_marker lines 408-413, _occurrence_block lines 520-522 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A command containing a line of four or more backticks can terminate the fixed four-backtick example match early, leaving family-marker text in the remainder to be trusted as issue metadata.
  WHY: On a legacy issue, a forged marker can override family derivation and route later prompts to the wrong issue; the reviewer describes exploitability as narrow and defense-in-depth.
